OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.1 Layers of the Skin (oxygen-poor blood is dark red)

legend.name: Right side
legend.meaning: Dark red: blood low in oxygen. Diagrams often show it blue, but blood is never blue.

legend.name: Left side
legend.meaning: Bright red: blood full of oxygen

steps.title: Heart muscle
steps.instruction: Trace the outside of the heart.

note.text: Your heart is a muscle about the size of your fist. It squeezes about once a second to pump blood all around your body.

steps.title: Right side
steps.instruction: Trace the two chambers on the left of the picture.

note.text: These are the heart's right side: it faces you, so its right is on your left. Blood from the body comes in here, then is pumped to the lungs.

steps.title: Left side
steps.instruction: Trace the two chambers on the right of the picture.

note.text: Blood full of oxygen comes back from the lungs into the left side. Its strong lower chamber pumps it out to the whole body.

steps.title: Blood flow
steps.instruction: Draw the four arrows showing where blood comes in and goes out.

note.text: Valves between the chambers act like one-way doors: they stop blood flowing backward, so it always moves the same way.
note.remember: Valves keep blood moving one way.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: Color the heart. Blood low in oxygen is dark red; blood full of oxygen is bright red.

steps.title: Name the chambers
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered chamber.

mistakes.Left atrium: The heart faces you, so its right side is on your left. This is the right atrium.

mistakes.Right atrium: The heart faces you, so its left side is on your right. This is the left atrium.

commonMistakes.Lung: The lungs are beside the heart, not inside it. These are the heart's four chambers.

steps.hint: Top chambers are atria; bottom chambers are ventricles.

steps.title: Blood's path
steps.instruction: Tap the places in order, starting from the body.
steps.why: Blood from the body goes into the right side, which pumps it to the lungs for oxygen. It returns to the left side, which pumps it to the body.
steps.hint: Where does blood get its oxygen?

steps.title: Explain
steps.instruction: Think about what the heart does.
steps.question: Why does the heart send blood to the lungs before the rest of the body?

options.text: So the blood can pick up oxygen the body needs
options.feedback: Yes. In the lungs, blood picks up oxygen and drops off carbon dioxide. Then the left side pumps it to the body.
Blood visits the lungs to pick up oxygen, not to clean them.
The trip to the lungs is about oxygen: the body's cells need it to live.

options.text: Because the lungs pump the blood
options.feedback: The heart does the pumping. The lungs are where oxygen gets into the blood.
